neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were members of the Board of Trustees of a temple, conspired to kidnap and kill the chairman of the temple due to his intention to transfer them for misappropriation of funds. The accused kidnapped the victim and killed him, then disposed of the body to destroy evidence. The body was later recovered and identified through medical examination. The accused also set fire to the vehicle used in the crime and filed a false insurance claim, which was rejected. The prosecution established the victim's last seen with one of the accused, the recovery of the body, and the disposal of the body by the accused. The accused also misled the investigating agencies and had a strong motive for the murder due to financial concerns.

quotes.text: Dismissing the appeals, the Court HELD: 1. On analyzing the evidence and the judgments including the findings and conclusion recorded by both the Courts, there is no hesitation in upholding the order of conviction against accused Nos. 1, 2 and 5 (appellants), by the High Court.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused, particularly Nos. 1-5, conspired to kidnap and kill the Chairman of the temple due to his intention to transfer them for misappropriation of funds. The evidence included the last-seen theory, the disposal of the body, the recovery of the body, and the conduct of the accused, all pointing to their involvement in the crime.

quotes.text: The prosecution case that Chairman of Board of Trustee of the temple proposed to transfer Kotharis from the temple on account of misappropriation of funds from the temple by them - Kotharis and their henchmen-uppellants nos. 1-5 entered into conspiracy, kidnapped the Chairman and killed him.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was based on imagination and that there were other persons hostile to the deceased. They also claimed that the prosecution failed to prove the disproportionate assets of the accused and that the evidence was insufficient to establish guilt.

quotes.text: The appellants made fervent effort to persuade the court about the several other discrepancies, however, does not discredit the other clinching circumstances established by the prosecution, which completes the chain of events indicative of the involvement of the appellants in commission of the crime.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that conspiracy is rarely hatched in the open and can be inferred from the basic facts and circumstances proved beyond all reasonable doubts, excluding any other conclusion except that of the accused's complicity.

quotes.text: It is well settled that such a conspiracy is rarely hatched in the open. There need not be any direct evidence to establish the same. It can be a matter of inference drawn by the Court after considering whether the basic facts and circumstances on the basis of which inference is drawn have been proved beyond all reasonable doubts and that no other conclusion except that of the complicity of accused to have agreed to commit an offence is evident.
